title: The AI 100: benchmarks for the third supercycle
gist: Bessemer's inaugural AI 100 (successor to the Cloud 100) values the top 100 private AI companies at $3.6T, over 3x the 2025 Cloud 100, with extreme power-law concentration (frontier labs are 9% of names but 55% of value) and a record 57x average ARR multiple that Bessemer argues is actually cheap (~12x) on a growth-adjusted basis given 480% average growth. A survey of 300+ AI-natives expects frontier model convergence, persistent compute scarcity and value accruing to the application layer, with cybersecurity, biotech and physical AI flagged as the next frontier.

themes.theme: AI 100 valuation scale and power-law concentration

insights.claim: Bessemer's inaugural AI 100 ranking of top private AI companies is worth $3.6 trillion in aggregate private value, more than three times the $1.1 trillion 2025 Cloud 100 it replaces.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Private AI value now dwarfs the prior SaaS cohort; public-market AI exposure captures only a fraction of value being created privately.
insights.quote: A single year of AI-native company formation added more private value than a decade of cloud did.
insights.locator: TL;DR: the inaugural AI 100 by the numbers

insights.claim: The average AI 100 company is valued at $36 billion versus $11.2 billion for the 2025 Cloud 100, while the median AI 100 valuation is $9.3 billion versus $5 billion, showing a few giants drag the mean up.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Use medians, not means, to benchmark typical AI private-market valuations; the median still nearly doubled year over year.
insights.locator: The 2026 AI 100 at a glance

insights.claim: Frontier labs and foundation model builders are only 9% of AI 100 companies but hold 55% of the list's value ($1,974 billion), the most concentrated category in a decade of Bessemer benchmarking.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: AI private value is a power law; exposure to a handful of labs dominates any AI private-market index or fund return.
insights.locator: TL;DR: the inaugural AI 100 by the numbers

insights.claim: The AI 100 top ten — Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, Waymo, Cognition, Anduril, Ramp, Fireworks and ElevenLabs — average $250 billion in valuation and account for 70% of the list's total value, with Anthropic ranked first ahead of OpenAI.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Watch these names as likely IPO / secondary-market bellwethers; their marks drive most aggregate AI private value.
insights.locator: The top 10—Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks

insights.claim: The 2016 Cloud 100 cohort was worth $99 billion and grew to $1.1 trillion by 2025, and the AI 100 at $3.6 trillion is 36x the 2016 Cloud 100 value in a decade.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Frames AI as a step-change supercycle versus cloud; supports allocators sizing AI as a larger opportunity than SaaS.
insights.locator: Ten years ago, we published the first Cloud 100

insights.claim: Bessemer frames AI as the third tech supercycle after internet (near-zero distribution cost) and cloud (near-zero compute cost), arguing intelligence is a multi-trillion-dollar market that will exceed oil in size.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Signals top-tier VC conviction that AI is a larger TAM than prior platform shifts, sustaining aggressive private funding.
insights.quote: intelligence is going to be bigger as a market than oil.
insights.locator: The internet took distribution cost to near zero

insights.claim: AI-native companies entered Bessemer's Cloud 100 as a category in 2023 and became its most valuable category within two years, prompting replacement of the Cloud 100 with a dedicated AI 100.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Shows how quickly AI displaced SaaS as the center of private software value creation.
insights.quote: The list didn't evolve by choice; this cohort simply outgrew the measuring stick.
insights.locator: For a decade, the Cloud 100 was

insights.claim: AI 100 companies trade at a record 57x average ARR multiple, above the Cloud 100's 2021 ZIRP-era peak of 34x and the 2025 Cloud 100 average of 20x; the AI 100 median multiple is 23x.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Headline AI private multiples exceed the 2021 bubble peak; median-to-mean gap shows froth is concentrated in the largest names.
insights.locator: Last year the average Cloud 100 revenue multiple

insights.claim: The average AI 100 company grew ARR 480% year over year (about 6x the Cloud 100), the top ten averaged 306% and the median 275%, faster than any year the Cloud 100 ever recorded, whose growth stayed in a 55%-100% range for nine years.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Growth rates at scale are unprecedented; deceleration from these levels is the key risk to watch for valuation resets.
insights.locator: Average ARR growth is 480%

insights.claim: Bessemer argues that on a growth-adjusted basis the AI 100 is the cheapest cohort in recent history, at an average 12x growth-adjusted multiple, despite record headline ARR multiples.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Counters the AI-bubble narrative; the bull case hinges entirely on growth persisting, so track growth durability rather than multiples alone.
insights.quote: on a growth-adjusted basis, the AI 100 is the cheapest cohort in recent history, with an average 12x multiple on a growth-adjusted basis
insights.locator: For nine years, the Cloud 100 never left

insights.claim: Anthropic went from founding to roughly $70 billion in annualized revenue run rate in about five years, and Legora (#45) reached Centaur status ($100M ARR) within 18 months, adding its second $100 million of ARR in under six months.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Time-to-scale for AI-natives is compressing dramatically, both for labs and vertical applications like legal AI.
insights.locator: Looking ahead: trends across the AI ecosystem

insights.claim: The AI 100 spans companies with effectively no revenue alongside companies approaching $100 billion in ARR, scored on market leadership (35%), estimated valuation (30%), operating metrics (20%) and people and culture (15%).
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Ranking weights valuation and leadership heavily, so it reflects private-market sentiment as much as fundamentals.
insights.locator: TL;DR: the inaugural AI 100 by the numbers

themes.theme: Founder survey: model convergence and multi-model stacks

insights.claim: In a Bessemer survey of over 300 AI-native companies, 79% believe frontier model quality will converge within the next 2-3 years.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: If models commoditize, frontier lab pricing power erodes; this tension sits against labs holding 55% of list value.
insights.locator: As part of the application process

insights.claim: 57% of surveyed AI-native companies run the majority of workloads on closed frontier models today, but plan to diversify such that this share may fall to 36%, shifting to a mix of closed, open-weight and custom fine-tuned or trained models.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Bullish for inference, post-training and open-model serving providers; a share headwind for closed-model API vendors.
insights.quote: Many are acting on the belief that the future belongs to those who own their intelligence.
insights.locator: Most believe model quality will converge

insights.claim: Bessemer identifies the enablers of owned or custom intelligence as Fireworks, Together and Baseten (serving open and custom models), Applied Compute and Thinking Machines' Tinker (post-training), Mercor (expert training data), Fal (media generation), Databricks (models next to enterprise data), and Mistral and Cohere (sovereign weights).
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: A map of picks-and-shovels beneficiaries if enterprises shift away from single closed-model dependence.
insights.locator: And the companies making that possible

insights.claim: 85% of over 300 surveyed AI-native companies expect compute demand to continue outstripping supply.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Supports continued capex and pricing power for compute suppliers and GPU-backed lenders.
insights.locator: 85% of respondents expect demand

insights.claim: Over the past year an entire financing market has sprung up around GPUs, and more AI companies are moving to owning their own GPU fleets rather than renting because owning beats unpredictable rental rates and expensive prepays.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Watch GPU-backed debt markets and neocloud rental demand; a shift to ownership could pressure GPU rental providers' pricing.
insights.quote: owning is increasingly more attractive than unpredictable rental rates and expensive prepays
insights.locator: 85% of respondents expect demand

insights.claim: 87% of surveyed AI-native companies expect value to accrue to the application layer rather than to model providers.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Founder consensus favors apps over labs, contrasting with current value concentration in frontier labs.
insights.locator: 87% of the companies we surveyed

insights.claim: The AI 100 application layer is worth $629 billion across roughly 40 companies at an average valuation of $15.7 billion, well above the $9.3 billion list median.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Application-layer AI companies are already commanding above-median valuations, supporting investment outside the labs.
insights.locator: Value is accruing to the application layer

insights.claim: Data and agent infrastructure is the most represented of 14 AI 100 categories with 16 companies.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Agent and data infrastructure is the broadest cluster of scaled private AI companies.
insights.locator: Across 14 different categories

themes.theme: Next frontier: cybersecurity, biotech, physical AI

insights.claim: Bessemer believes cybersecurity, biotech and robotics are the biggest AI opportunities ahead, noting cybersecurity and biotech each have only three AI 100 companies and together represent under 3% of list value.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Underrepresented AI verticals where Bessemer expects new startup formation and future value creation.
insights.locator: The next frontier: cybersecurity, biotech, and physical AI

insights.claim: Physical AI accounts for 13 AI 100 companies with a cumulative $332 billion valuation (about 9% of list value), with some effectively pre-revenue such as Physical Intelligence, Mind Robotics and Bedrock, while Waymo is on the road and Saronic builds defense vessels.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Physical AI carries large valuations ahead of revenue; next year's list will test how fast pre-revenue robotics companies commercialize.
insights.quote: Next year’s list will tell us how fast the pre-revenue companies cross over.
insights.locator: Physical AI is the counterexample

insights.claim: Six AI 100 companies have each raised more than $10 billion — OpenAI ($224 billion), Anthropic ($130 billion), Databricks, Waymo, Prometheus and Anduril — with OpenAI and Anthropic together at $354 billion, about 80% of the six's combined total.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: AI leaders are extraordinarily capital-intensive, making them dependent on continued mega-round and debt financing.
insights.locator: Capital concentration in the AI 100

insights.claim: Excluding OpenAI and Anthropic, the average AI 100 company has raised $3.9 billion and the median about $1.09 billion, meaning making the list effectively requires over a billion dollars raised.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Capital requirements to reach AI scale are far higher than in SaaS, favoring mega-fund investors and raising dilution risk.
insights.quote: To make this list, you’ve already raised more than a billion dollars, which was rare just five years ago.
insights.locator: Excluding the two labs

insights.claim: 14 of the AI 100 companies were founded by someone who previously worked at another AI 100 company; OpenAI alumni founded Anthropic, Thinking Machines, Safe Superintelligence, Applied Compute, TypeSafe and Periodic Labs, and Stripe alumni founded Render, Physical Intelligence and Chai Discovery.
insights.speaker: Bessemer Venture Partners
insights.so_what: Alumni networks of AI 100 companies are a leading indicator for sourcing next year's breakout startups.
insights.quote: It’s clear that great businesses beget great founders.
insights.locator: Great businesses beget great founders
